set.st: The night operator was convicted of taking about $9,000 from the depot safe at Abbotsford on 18 May 1891: $8,000 sent by the Seymour Bank, Chippewa Falls, to the State Bank of Phillips, about $1,000 more and two jewelry packages (Northern Pacific Express). His footprints were found under the depot the next morning, "very likely seeking a safe hiding place", and he was in the woods that morning walking to Colby. He got 5 years at Waupun, and "the money has never been found". In June 1892 a rumor said it had been found buried near Abbotsford, with a local family "very flush with money". The pin marks the railroad junction area where the depot likely stood, not the spot itself.
